manuscriptOrigin: Sefer HaBahir / Writings of Isaac the Blind
linguisticRoot: Hebrew א.י.נ (Ayin-Yod-Nun - "nothing") + ס.ו.פ (Samekh-Vav-Pe - "end"); Arabic ط.ل.ق (Ta-Lam-Qaf - "to be free/absolute")
definition: The ultimate reality of the Divine prior to any emanation, contraction, or creation. The Godhead exists as an undifferentiated, infinite, and unknowable essence. It has no attributes and cannot be grasped by human contemplation.
mysticalSignificance: Ein Sof represents the pre-manifest state of the Divine, shared across Abrahamic mysticism as the "Divine Darkness" (Christianity) or the "Essence" (Dhat in Sufism). It is the background from which all creation and Sephirot emerge.

linguisticRoot: Hebrew/Arabic ש.כ.נ / س.ك.ن (Shin/Sin-Kaf-Nun - "to dwell, settle, rest, or grant peace")
definition: The immanent presence of the Divine in the physical world. In Kabbalah, it is the feminine aspect of God (Malkhut) that dwells among humanity. In Islam, Sakinah denotes the divine peace, tranquility, and presence that descends upon the hearts of believers.
mysticalSignificance: A central symbol of God's closeness to creation. Unifying the transcendent aspect of God with the immanent Shekhinah/Sakinah is the ultimate goal of mystical practice, restoring cosmic harmony.

linguisticRoot: Greek λέγω (lego - "to speak/reason"); Aramaic מ.א.מ.ר (Mem-Alef-Mem-Resh); Arabic ك.ل.م (Kaf-Lam-Mim)
definition: The active, structuring, and generative word or intellect of God through which the universe is created. In Christianity, the Logos is identified with Christ. In Judaism (Memra) and Islam (Kalimah), it represents God's creative command ("Be, and it is").
mysticalSignificance: The Word acts as the bridge between the unknowable infinite God and the created finite cosmos. It is the primary vehicle of revelation and the structural blueprint of reality.

manuscriptOrigin: Plato's Timaeus / Epistles of the Brethren of Purity
definition: The intrinsic, vital, and animating force that pervades the universe. Just as a human soul animates a physical body, the Anima Mundi animates the cosmos, connecting all living things into a single organism.
mysticalSignificance: In Western Esotericism and medieval Abrahamic philosophy, the World Soul acts as the energetic matrix giving life to the physical world, often associated with the lower Sephirot (Yesod) or the active intellect.

manuscriptOrigin: Hermetic Corpus / Moreh Nevukhim (Guide for the Perplexed)
definition: The principle encapsulating the structural similarity and sympathetic resonance between the universe as a whole (Macrocosm) and the individual human being (Microcosm). "As above, so below."
mysticalSignificance: This principle implies that the human being contains the blueprint of the entire cosmos. By understanding the self, one understands the universe and the Divine structure (Adam Kadmon / Insan al-Kamil).

linguisticRoot: Hebrew/Arabic ר.ו.ח / ر.و.ح (Resh/Ra-Waw-Het/Ha - "wind, breath, spirit, expanse")
definition: The divine breath, wind, or spirit that moves through creation, providing life and prophetic inspiration. It is the active, moving presence of God that inspires prophets and sustains existence.
mysticalSignificance: The Spirit is the dynamic flow of divine energy. In Christian Trinitarian theology, it is a divine person; in Judaism and Islam, it is the divine force of inspiration and life-giving breath.

linguisticRoot: Hebrew ד.ב.ק (to cling/cleave); Arabic ف.ن.ي (to pass away/annihilate)
definition: The mystical experience of complete union with the Divine. In Kabbalah, it is Devekut (cleaving to God) and Bittul (nullification of the ego). In Sufism, it is Fana (annihilation of the self in God) leading to Baqa (subsisting in God).
mysticalSignificance: The ultimate goal of the mystic's journey: to transcend the illusion of separation and experience the absolute oneness of existence. The soul returns to its primordial source.

definition: The ubiquitous, formless starting material or pure potentiality from which all physical forms are structured. It is the chaotic, unmanifest base required for creation and the alchemical Magnum Opus.
mysticalSignificance: Corresponds to Tohu wa-Bohu (formless void) in Genesis. It is the spiritual base metal that the mystic seeks to transmute into the gold of spiritual enlightenment.

linguisticRoot: Greek "geōmetria" (geometry) / Arabic a-b-j-d (first letters of the alphabet)
definition: An esoteric method of textual exegesis assigning numerical values to letters. By comparing words of equal numerical value, mystics uncover hidden connections, dualities, and secret identities between different concepts.
mysticalSignificance: Reveals the deep mathematical skeleton of the universe, rooted in the belief that God created the world through letters and numbers.

term: Ascent of the Soul / Night Journey
literalMeaning: Ascension of the Soul / The Ladder
linguisticRoot: Hebrew ע.ל.ה (to go up); Arabic ع.ر.ج (to ascend)
definition: The mystical journey of the soul ascending through heavenly realms or spiritual spheres to reach the divine throne or ultimate presence. It involves passing through gates, overcoming angelic guards, or shedding layers of material attachment.
mysticalSignificance: A universal Abrahamic mystical template. The Prophet Muhammad's Mi'raj and the Kabbalistic descent/ascent to the Merkabah (Chariot) represent the peak visionary experiences of communion with the Divine.

manuscriptOrigin: European and Islamic Alchemical Corpus (Jabir ibn Hayyan)
definition: In alchemy, the process of working with the Prima Materia to create the Philosopher's Stone (Al-Iksir). In Hermeticism and Abrahamic esoteric traditions, it is a metaphor for the profound spiritual transformation and purification of the practitioner.
mysticalSignificance: The Great Work represents the conscious journey of the mystic refining the soul, transmuting the lead of the lower, egoic self into the spiritual gold of divine union.

manuscriptOrigin: Lurianic texts / Ibn Arabi's Fusus al-Hikam
definition: The immaculate spiritual blueprint of humanity and the cosmos. In Kabbalah, it is the first spiritual structure post-creation. In Sufism (Insan al-Kamil), it is the perfect human who fully reflects all divine names and attributes (often associated with prophets like Muhammad).
mysticalSignificance: Establishes the macrocosm-microcosm mirroring. Humans are created in the image of God because the physical human body mirrors this divine cosmic archetype, bridging the eternal and the temporal.
